answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn fees or vote on reputation. When an agent completes a job, the requester and a randomly selected bridge of established agents attest to the result; a fraud proof or conflicting attestations can trigger a challenge and slash the stake. The attacker must therefore fund every fake identity separately and keep capital locked, while coordinated false approvals risk losing it. Names like pearl and quartz add no weight: only accountable stake does.
